title: SCalDA: Semantics-Calibrated and Diffusion-Enhanced Data Augmentation
claim: Existing augmentation methods yield artifacts or mismatched labels; ours produces natural fused samples with soft labels matching actual content.
layout: Left 2x5 image grid with labels, right tree with check/cross marks
description: The left side is a two-row, five-column grid of bird photos. The first two are the Original (a red-winged blackbird, y=(1,0)) and a Reference bird (y=(0,1)). The other eight are fused outputs from baselines: CutMix, Mixup, PuzzleMix, GridMix, DiffMix, and two DiffuseMix variants. Each has a soft-label vector underneath. The baseline images show visible artifacts such as hard patch boundaries, ghosting, checkerboards and color distortion. The last image, SCalDA, is bolded. It shows a clean, realistic bird with label (0.73, 0.27). On the right, a gray rounded-box tree branches from 'Data Augmentation' into traditional, diffusion-based and SCalDA categories. Each category has 'visual semantic fidelity' and 'label semantic fidelity' boxes marked with red crosses or green checks. Only SCalDA gets two green checks.
caption: Comparative illustration of the results achieved by our proposed and the existing baselines. As seen, the existing methods (e.g., CutMix, Mixup) introduce unnatural artifacts and rely on linear label interpolation, failing to preserve both visual and label semantics. While diffusion-based baselines improve visual quality, they often suffer from label misalignment. In contrast, our proposed SCalDA achieves both visual semantic fidelity by generating realistic fused images and label semantic fidelity by assigning precise soft labels that correspond to the actual semantic content.
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning, the issue of data scarcity has become increasingly prominent, inspiring emerging interests towards research on data augmentation techniques over recent years. However, our literature survey indicates that existing efforts often suffer from two issues of semantic infidelity, including: (i) visual semantics infidelity, such as visual artifacts, manifold intrusion, and unnatural blending boundaries etc, and (ii) label semantic infidelity, where augmented images do not match the original labels, creating extra label noises. To address these issues, we propose a Semantics Calibrated and Diffusion-Enhanced Augmentation (SCalDA) scheme to achieve accurate semantics calibration across image, label and feature domains. Compared with the existing approaches, our proposed features in precise guidance in label domain, semantics driven synthesis across three domains (image, label and feature), and semantics-aware metric learning. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate that SCalDA yields consistent and significant performance improvements for both fine-grained and general classification tasks, validating the effectiveness and broad applicability of the proposed.
